authority: Capability inventory only. Task state remains in system/roadmap.json and state/events.jsonl; live verification is source-bound.

items.title: Entry point
items.acceptance: One command reports environment, changes, tasks, and evidence.

items.title: Task routing
items.acceptance: Five routes name small working sets.

items.title: Repository map
items.acceptance: Documentation distinguishes overlays, pilots, task authority, and local artifacts.

items.title: Supported commands
items.acceptance: Setup, verify, stress, status, and explain have public parsers.

items.title: Dependency setup
items.acceptance: Setup locates or installs the pinned Bun runtime.

items.title: Upstream acquisition
items.acceptance: Setup fetches and checks the exact upstream pin.

items.title: Workspace discovery
items.acceptance: Local configuration retains the target path.

items.title: Environment diagnostics
items.acceptance: Doctor exposes missing prerequisites before verification.

items.title: Runtime consistency
items.acceptance: CI and setup read the same toolchain manifest.

items.title: Cleanliness checks
items.acceptance: Status reports staged, tracked, and untracked changes.

items.title: Safe resumability
items.acceptance: Setup preserves unknown edits and accepts its prior overlay outputs.

items.title: Guarantee map
items.acceptance: Law catalog connects each formal claim to its model and witnesses.

items.title: Evidence classification
items.acceptance: Receipts retain their required evidence kind and scope.

items.title: Trust boundary
items.acceptance: Controller, producers, runtime, Git, and host assumptions are explicit.

items.title: Deployment status
items.acceptance: Local verification and external enforcement remain distinct.

items.title: Law definitions
items.acceptance: Every law has premises, positive case, and forbidden case.

items.title: Non-vacuity
items.acceptance: Useful acceptance and concrete positive cases remain executable.

items.title: Negative coverage
items.acceptance: Compiled false claims are distinguished from documented forbidden cases.

items.title: Model correspondence
items.acceptance: All 54 finite decisions execute in Bend and match Python.

items.title: Scope boundaries
items.acceptance: Unsupported formats, external effects, and crash assumptions are stated.

items.title: Amendments
items.acceptance: Policy change procedure uses prior authority and cannot exempt its own patch.

items.title: Public API
items.acceptance: Admission exports stable named constructors and operations.

items.title: Data structures
items.acceptance: Validated canonical immutable documents prevent nested mutation.

items.title: Construction
items.acceptance: Builders construct policies, manifests, and bundles.

items.title: Serialization
items.acceptance: Strict parsing and canonical serialization are shared.

items.title: Error reporting
items.acceptance: Stable decision codes accompany descriptive reasons.

items.title: Decision explanation
items.acceptance: Each evidence domain has a separate outcome.

items.title: Inspection
items.acceptance: Manifest inspection and field-level comparison are available.

items.title: Dry runs
items.acceptance: Plans disclose intended refs without mutating them.

items.title: Timeout recovery
items.acceptance: Reconciliation preserves uncertainty and never grants blind retries.

items.title: Repository identity
items.acceptance: Controller-owned mapping is explicit and checked before mutation.

items.title: Policy loading
items.acceptance: Immutable policy construction validates the controller-supplied content.

items.title: Producer integration
items.acceptance: A bounded command producer retains bytes and signs its bounded-test result.

items.title: Key handling
items.acceptance: Signing is confined to explicit producer calls; verification trust is documented.

items.title: Examples
items.acceptance: Disposable demo exercises producer, gate, commit, replay, and reconciliation.

items.title: Proof repetition
items.acceptance: Exact generated cases replace manual maintenance of repeated branches.

items.title: Generated proofs
items.acceptance: Generator --check rejects drift.

items.title: Proof inventory
items.acceptance: An exact nine-law inventory rejects omissions and duplicates.

items.title: Focused verification
items.acceptance: Named scopes expose component-level checks.

items.title: Full verification
items.acceptance: One bounded command aggregates required checks.

items.title: Skipped tests
items.acceptance: Unexpected skipped or empty suites fail the gate.

items.title: Stress coverage
items.acceptance: Campaign declares finite dimensions, mutations, and deadlines.

items.title: Mutation maintenance
items.acceptance: Every named mutation validates its unique source anchor.

items.title: Mutation diagnostics
items.acceptance: Expected test failure identifies detection of each fault.

items.title: Counterexample retention
items.acceptance: Minimal reproducers and law references have a supported capture command.

items.title: Concurrency coverage
items.acceptance: Bounded repeated races verify a single winning Git transaction.

items.title: Crash coverage
items.acceptance: Lost acknowledgements are tested and distinguished from power-loss durability.

items.title: Evidence freshness
items.acceptance: Source, tests, configuration, runtime, upstream, and logs bind run results.

items.title: Result summaries
items.acceptance: Small summaries point to full per-step logs.

items.title: Evidence retention
items.acceptance: New bulky runs remain local or in CI artifacts; committed records preserve useful history.

items.title: CI topology
items.acceptance: Jobs and their claims are documented; required enforcement is separately inspected.

items.title: Check enforcement
items.acceptance: Read-only host inspection distinguishes workflow existence from host rules.

items.title: Merge candidate identity
items.acceptance: CI records evaluated source and upstream identity on merge-group events.

items.title: Workflow protection
items.acceptance: Policy procedure identifies the complete checker dependency boundary.

items.title: Remote publishing
items.acceptance: Prepared packets support CLI and connected-GitHub transport.

items.title: Publication verification
items.acceptance: Exact remote commit tree is compared with local content.

items.title: PR descriptions
items.acceptance: Publication prepares the body from current verification metadata.

items.title: CI waiting
items.acceptance: Bounded watch distinguishes pending from completed checks.

items.title: Completion state
items.acceptance: Task authority, local evidence, remote CI, merge, and deployment are separate.

items.title: Status duplication
items.acceptance: Capability views render from one catalog and task views reuse the existing journal.

items.title: Residual obligations
items.acceptance: Each open boundary names consequence, probe, and reopen trigger.

items.title: Historical claims
items.acceptance: Source-bound records distinguish historical success from freshness.

items.title: Change impact
items.acceptance: Changed paths map to declared checks with a full-suite fallback.

items.title: Task completion
items.acceptance: Existing journal requires retained fresh evidence to close tasks.

items.title: Resource limits
items.acceptance: Total and per-step budgets stop bounded runs; no remote workers start.

items.title: Recovery instructions
items.acceptance: Interrupted runs retain completed steps and a safe reverify command.
